messages:
Leo: Ok heads-up 1: ACME Health wants to join the design-partner cohort but insists on private deployment (VPC) and a 99.9% SLA for inference. they're offering to sign an LOI if we accept those terms for the pilot.
Ava: Big ask. We need to decide if this is a strategic DP or a separate enterprise pilot. Different onboarding, ops load, and legal risk.
Jordan: Technically doable for a short pilot if we scope it: limited VPC image, single-region, timeboxed (6 weeks) and access controls. But we need runbook automation and an ops contact.
Sam: Ops note: provisioning a private env per DP adds ~2-3 dev-ops hours plus monitoring config. We should cap to 1 private DP per quarter unless we allocate dedicated infra engineering hours.
Priya: Legal: a 99.9% SLA triggers enterprise contract language (credits, breach remedies). For a pilot we can offer an "operational commitment" with limited remedies and a termination right, not full commercial SLA. I'll draft pilot terms and a consent clause for anonymized telemetry.
Maya: From a growth perspective, ACME Health would be a high-signal partner. If they surface compliance/login patterns and evaluation prompts it could guide product work. But we should require specific success metrics tied to product outcomes, not just uptime.
Diego: Suggest success criteria mix: 1) integration: customer runs N sample workflows end-to-end; 2) performance: median latency below X ms for target calls; 3) quality: customer eval set passes agreed metrics; 4) feedback cadence: 3 structured sessions + weekly async notes.
Leo: Customer prefers 2-week onboarding and then 4-week pilot. They're ok with "pilot SLA" if we commit to quick remediation windows and a dedicated escalation contact.
Ava: Proposal: treat as "Enterprise Design Partner" with these guardrails:
- Private VPC deployment, single region, timeboxed 6 weeks
- Operational commitment (not commercial SLA): incident response target 4h, remediation plan within 24h
- Success criteria: integration runbook completed, perf baseline uploaded, 3 feedback sessions, and acceptance criteria on quality tests
- Limit incentives to credits + onboarding support hours; no long-term revenue concessions yet
- Legal pilot terms: limited liability for pilot period, consent for anonymized telemetry, clear exit triggers
Priya: That aligns. I'll prepare a 1-page pilot addendum and checkbox language for telemetry. Also will flag any data residency clauses from their security team.
Jordan: I'll draft a minimal infra checklist and an automated perf test script we can run during onboarding (10 sample calls, capture p50/p95/p99). It will upload a CSV to our analytics bucket.
Sam: I'll reserve a dedicated ops slot for the pilot window and coordinate rotation so on-call isn't overloaded. Can support provisioning in ~3 business days once security docs are signed.
Maya: For recruitment messaging and internal comms, let's label this "Enterprise DP - VPC Pilot" and keep product PMs looped for weekly syncs. Also capture customer pain points to map asks to roadmap items.
Diego: Measurement schema I'll publish: participant_id (customer-dp), deployment_type, region, onboarding_start_ts, onboarding_complete_ts, perf_p50_ms, perf_p95_ms, feedback_sessions_count, quality_pass_rate, nps_30.
onboarding-bot: Reminder: create entry in dp-beta-queue with tag "enterprise-vpc" and attach pilot addendum when available. :robot_face:
Ava: Next steps: Leo to confirm LOI language with ACME Health; Priya drafts pilot addendum; Jordan builds perf test script; Sam schedules ops window; Diego defines measurement tags; I'll assemble success criteria doc and run internal risk review. If everyone ok, we reply to Leo and ask customer for security contacts and LOI draft.
Leo: I'll chase LOI and security contacts today. ACME wants to start onboarding asap if we can commit to the pilot cadence.
Ava: Agreed. Let's aim to have pilot addendum + ops slot locked in by EOW so we can start the first wave next week. Any objections?
Priya: No objections. I'll ping legal review channel when draft is ready.
Jordan: No objections, will start the script.
Sam: No objections, I'll block the calendar.
Maya: Excited to see the data we get from an enterprise DP.
Diego: Same. I'll prep the tiny sample CSV schema for the analytics doc.
Ava: Great 1: I'll reply to Leo and update this thread with the LOI checklist. Thanks all.
